questions.explanation: Most Arunachal soils are acidic because of high rainfall that leaches bases (Ca, Mg, K). In acid soils Fe and Al are soluble and fix phosphate as insoluble Fe/Al phosphates, so P is the classic deficient nutrient. Liming to raise pH (~6–6.5) and using rock phosphate (which dissolves well in acid soil) are standard corrections.
questions.hook: Acid soil = 'FeAl' steals P. Lime gives it back.

optionNotes.A: Correct. R is exactly the reason for low P in acid soils.
optionNotes.B: R is not a side fact; P fixation by Fe/Al is the direct cause of low P availability.
optionNotes.C: R is true. P fixation by Fe and Al is textbook acid-soil chemistry (in alkaline soils P is fixed by Ca instead).
optionNotes.D: A is true. Low P (along with Ca, Mg, Mo) is typical of acid soils, while Al, Fe and Mn can reach toxic levels.

optionNotes.C: Correct pairing.

questions.explanation: Paclobutrazol (PBZ) is a triazole growth retardant that blocks gibberellin biosynthesis. Less GA means less vegetative growth and more flower-bud initiation, so it is used to induce flowering in alternate-bearing cultivars and in off-years. It is applied to the soil around the collar region of the tree.
questions.hook: PBZ = 'Put Brakes on Zooming growth' → GA down, flowers up.

optionNotes.A: Opposite effect. High GA promotes vegetative growth and actually suppresses flowering in mango.
optionNotes.B: Correct. PBZ is an anti-gibberellin (triazole).
optionNotes.C: That describes ethephon (2-chloroethylphosphonic acid), used for pineapple flowering and fruit ripening.
optionNotes.D: PBZ is not a cytokinin. Hydrogen cyanamide (Dormex) is the common bud-dormancy breaker in grape and temperate fruits.

questions.explanation: Embryo rescue saves young embryos that would abort, as in wide crosses or seedless grape breeding. Anther (and pollen) culture gives haploids, which are doubled to make homozygous lines quickly. The apical meristem is usually free of virus, so meristem-tip culture gives virus-free stock (potato, banana, sweet potato). Protoplast fusion joins cells of two species to make somatic hybrids, as in citrus and potato. Biotech tools are a new 2026 syllabus line.
questions.hook: Embryo = Emergency rescue; Anther = Alone (haploid); Meristem = Medicine (virus-free); Protoplast = Partner (hybrid).

right: 4. Recovering hybrids from wide or seedless × seedless crosses

optionNotes.A: Swaps anther and meristem culture. Anthers give haploids; meristem gives virus-free plants.
optionNotes.B: Reverses embryo rescue and protoplast fusion. Somatic hybrids come from fusing protoplasts, not from rescuing embryos.
optionNotes.C: Gives anther culture the wide-cross job. Wide crosses need embryo rescue; anthers give haploids.
optionNotes.D: Correct pairing.

questions.explanation: pH measures only active acidity in the soil solution. Most acidity sits in reserve on exchange sites (Al3+, H+), so heavy, high-CEC or organic soils resist pH change and need more lime. That is why buffer methods such as SMP are used to work out lime requirement. Acid soils are widespread in Arunachal, so this is a likely question.
questions.hook: pH is the tip; reserve acidity is the iceberg. More clay or OM means a bigger iceberg and more lime.

optionNotes.A: Correct: buffer capacity (reserve acidity) explains why lime need differs at the same pH.
optionNotes.B: Wrong: R is the actual reason for A, not an unrelated fact.
optionNotes.C: Wrong: R is true. Clay and humus raise CEC and therefore buffering.
optionNotes.D: Wrong: A is true. Lime requirement is set by pH together with buffer capacity, not by pH alone.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A

optionNotes.D: Correct: SSR / microsatellite – co-dominant, highly polymorphic. RFLP is also co-dominant.

questions.explanation: HLB is caused by a phloem-limited bacterium (Candidatus Liberibacter asiaticus) spread by the psyllid Diaphorina citri and by infected budwood. No spray cures an infected tree. optionNotes.A: Recommended: infected budwood is a main way HLB spreads, so certified nursery stock under nets is the first line of defence.
optionNotes.B: Recommended: the Asian citrus psyllid (Diaphorina citri) is the vector. Imidacloprid/thiamethoxam at new flush is standard.
optionNotes.C: Recommended: roguing removes the source of the bacterium for psyllids.
optionNotes.D: NOT recommended (correct answer): copper oxychloride is a contact bactericide/fungicide used for canker and Phytophthora. It cannot reach or kill the phloem-limited HLB bacterium.

questions.explanation: In polyembryonic citrus (and mango), extra embryos arise from the nucellus, a sporophytic maternal tissue. Since there is no fertilisation, they are genetic copies of the mother plant, so they are true-to-type. Most viruses do not pass into them through the seed. This is why nucellar lines are used for vigorous, virus-free rootstocks. It was asked in HDO 2022.
questions.hook: Nucellar = 'Nu-Clone' (mother's copy, minus the virus).

optionNotes.A: Correct: both are true, and R (an apomictic, maternal origin) explains A.
optionNotes.B: Wrong: R is the direct reason for A.
optionNotes.C: Wrong: R is true. Nucellar embryony is a form of adventive embryony (sporophytic apomixis).
optionNotes.D: Wrong: A is true. Nucellar seedlings are uniform and true-to-type.

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A

questions.explanation: Wither-tip or anthracnose of citrus is caused by the fungus Colletotrichum gloeosporioides. Twigs dry from the tip downwards, and the fungus also causes fruit rot and stem-end drop. It is one of the factors behind citrus decline (dieback) in old, poorly managed mandarin orchards of the NE, including Arunachal. Control: prune dead wood and spray copper oxychloride or carbendazim.
questions.hook: Colletotrichum = Cuts the tip: twigs WITHER from the TIP.

optionNotes.C: Correct: Colletotrichum gloeosporioides causes wither-tip / anthracnose.
optionNotes.D: Wrong: Phytophthora spp. (P. nicotianae var. parasitica, P. citrophthora) cause foot rot / gummosis at the collar region.

questions.explanation: Seed multiplies in a fixed chain: Nucleus → Breeder → Foundation → Certified. So foundation seed is grown from breeder seed. It is produced by State Seed Corporations, NSC or SAU farms, and certified by the State Seed Certification Agency, which gives it a WHITE tag.
questions.hook: N-B-F-C = 'No Brother Fails Certification'. Foundation comes right after Breeder.

optionNotes.A: Correct: breeder seed (golden-yellow tag) is the parent of foundation seed (white tag).
optionNotes.B: Wrong: nucleus seed is the purest, first handful kept by the original breeder. It gives rise to BREEDER seed, not foundation seed.
optionNotes.C: Wrong: certified seed (blue tag) is produced FROM foundation seed. It is the last stage and goes to farmers.
optionNotes.D: Wrong: truthfully labelled (TL) seed is sold under the producer's own label, without certification. It is not part of the certification chain (its label colour is opal green; verify).

questions.explanation: Most citrus seeds hold several embryos: one zygotic and many nucellar (polyembryony). Pummelo is the well-known exception; it is monoembryonic, so its seedlings are zygotic and vary. Rough lemon and Rangpur lime are highly polyembryonic, which is why they make uniform, true-to-type rootstock seedlings. Khasi mandarin, the orange of Arunachal and the NE, is also polyembryonic.
questions.hook: Pummelo is the 'Plain One': ONE embryo, no nucellar babies.

optionNotes.A: Wrong: rough lemon (C. jambhiri) is highly polyembryonic; a vigorous rootstock suited to light soils.
optionNotes.B: Correct: pummelo (C. grandis / C. maxima) is monoembryonic, so it is useful as a female parent in hybridisation.
optionNotes.C: Wrong: Rangpur lime (C. limonia) is polyembryonic; a drought-tolerant rootstock, also tolerant to tristeza.
optionNotes.D: Wrong: Khasi mandarin (C. reticulata) is polyembryonic. NE growers raise it from seed, and the nucellar seedlings are true-to-type.

questions.explanation: SALT grows field and horticultural crops in strips between double hedgerows of nitrogen-fixing shrubs planted along the contour. The hedgerows check soil erosion and supply green-leaf manure. It was developed in the Philippines and is promoted for NE hills as a settled alternative to jhum, together with contour bunding, bench terraces and horticulture-based agroforestry.
questions.hook: SALT the slope: Strips Along Lines of Trees (contour hedgerows).

optionNotes.A: Correct: SALT = contour hedgerows of N-fixing shrubs + crops in alleys; it reduces erosion.
optionNotes.B: Wrong: a shorter jhum cycle is the PROBLEM. It does not let the fallow restore fertility, so soils degrade.
optionNotes.C: Wrong: up-and-down cultivation speeds up runoff and erosion. Hill farming must be done ACROSS the slope (on the contour).
optionNotes.D: Wrong: trees such as Nepal alder in jhum fallows fix N and conserve soil; removing them speeds up degradation.

optionNotes.C: Wrong: Ralstonia is a bacterium causing Moko, not Panama wilt (Panama is fungal, Fusarium).

questions.explanation: Kiwi does not change skin colour at maturity, so harvest is judged by TSS: about 6.2% (minimum) to 6.5° Brix. optionNotes.C: Wrong: R is true. Kiwi is climacteric (like apple, banana, guava), unlike non-climacteric citrus and pineapple.

questions.explanation: Nucellar embryos arise from the nucellus (maternal tissue), not from fertilisation, so the seedlings are clones of the mother tree. Most citrus viruses are not seed-transmitted, so nucellar lines start virus-free. They are very vigorous but stay juvenile (thorny, late bearing) for years. This is why polyembryonic types are used as uniform rootstocks (2022 HDO asked nucellar seedlings).
questions.hook: NUCELLUS = MUM's cells: copy of mum, clean of virus, but a thorny teenager.

optionNotes.A: True: nucellar embryony is a form of apomixis (adventive embryony), so seedlings are maternal clones.
optionNotes.B: True: viruses rarely pass through seed, so nucellar clones are a classic route to virus-free citrus stock.
optionNotes.C: True: nucellar seedlings show juvenile traits – vigour, thorns, delayed bearing.
optionNotes.D: Correct: all three features apply. (Pummelo and citron are monoembryonic, so they give no nucellar seedlings.)

options.text: Genetically identical (true-to-type) to the mother plant

questions.explanation: Anthurium (family Araceae) has tiny true flowers packed on a finger-like spadix; the glossy coloured 'flower' is the spathe, a modified bract. Cut anthurium has a long vase life (asked in HDO 2022) and is grown under shade nets/polyhouses in the NE hills, including Arunachal.
questions.hook: SPATHE = SHIELD (heart-shaped bract); SPADIX = STICK with the real flowers.

optionNotes.A: Wrong: the spadix is the central spike that bears the tiny true flowers.
optionNotes.B: Correct: the spathe is a large coloured bract surrounding the spadix.
optionNotes.C: Wrong: tepals are undifferentiated perianth parts (as in lily, tulip).
optionNotes.D: Wrong: petals are part of the corolla; aroids have no showy petals.

questions.explanation: Kiwi is a vigorous, dioecious, deciduous climber, so it needs a strong overhead support. The T-bar and the pergola (bower/overhead trellis) are the standard systems; male vines are interplanted with females for pollination. Ziro valley is Arunachal's best-known kiwi belt and the state has organic-certified kiwi.
questions.hook: Kiwi climbs to the ROOF: T-bar or pergola.

optionNotes.A: Wrong: Kniffin (four-arm, two-wire) is a grape training system.
optionNotes.B: Wrong: head system is low-cost grape training for low-vigour vines.
optionNotes.C: Wrong: espalier trains trees flat against a wall/wire, as in apple and pear in small gardens.
optionNotes.D: Correct: T-bar and pergola are the standard kiwi trellises.

questions.explanation: The rhizomes and roots of kutki contain the bitter iridoid glycosides picroside I and II (kutkin), used as a liver tonic and in jaundice. It grows in alpine zones and is over-harvested, so it is a conservation priority. The syllabus lists Picrorhiza among AP's high-altitude MAPs (Tawang, West Kameng).
questions.hook: KUTKI = KUT the jaundice: bitter root for the liver.

optionNotes.A: Wrong: that is jatamansi (Nardostachys jatamansi) – rhizome oil, sedative.
optionNotes.B: Wrong: taxol (paclitaxel) comes from Taxus (Himalayan yew).
optionNotes.C: Correct: kutki's picrosides are hepatoprotective.
optionNotes.D: Wrong: quinine comes from Cinchona bark.

questions.explanation: Climacteric fruits (banana, apple, kiwi, guava) can ripen after harvest because of the ethylene/respiration burst, so they are picked mature-green and ripened in chambers (about 100 ppm ethylene, 18–20 °C) or dipped in ethephon. Non-climacteric fruits (citrus, pineapple, grape) do not ripen after picking and must be harvested ripe.
questions.hook: CLIMACTERIC = CLIMBS after harvest: pick green, ripen later.
